newsitem.title: UK: Granada extends gains on hotel disposals.
newsitem.headline: Granada extends gains on hotel disposals.

text.p: Shares in British media and leisure company Granada Group Plc extended recent gains on Thursday as the market welcomed progress on its luxury hotel disposal plans.
Granada shares, which added 8p on Wednesday when the sale of the George V hotel in Paris for 104 million stg was announced, had firmed a further 5p to 887 1/2p by 1130 GMT.

"This is an exceptional price for a hotel that needs considerable investment,' said analyst Greg Feehely of Kleinwort Benson. Saudi Prince al-Waleed bin Talal is buying the Parisian property for some 12 million stg above book value.

The sale is the second in the planned disposal of 17 luxury Exclusive hotels acquired as part of the 3.9 billion takeover of Forte earlier this year. Granada sold London's Hyde Park Hotel for 86 million stg last month, 15 million stg over book value.
"The two they have sold are ones in which there was considerable interest. They may struggle to achieve book value on some of the ones at the tail-end,' added Feehely.
Kleinwort expects Granada to raise around 850 million stg from the sales, a gain of 50 million stg on book value.

There has recently been speculation that Granada might decide to hold on to the most valuable Exclusive hotel, London's Grosvenor House, if bids fail to match the 350 million stg it is reportedly seeking.
Feehely said he would be unhappy if Granada opted not to sell such a substantial asset.
